title: Workplace Cafe Management Program: Late Charges on Unpaid Cafe Invoicing
content:
A client holding a Workplace Cafe Management Program contract whose cafe invoicing has stood unpaid beyond the grace days allowed on that contract stands to carry a late charge for the delay. This is the ordinary arrears position on a site: the cafe keeps serving, the management fees keep being invoiced, and the money owed on the contract is not settled.

The result the policy governs is a late charge raised on that contract. It is a contractual charge booked onto the contract's ledger, dated the day it is raised, recorded against the billing period in which it is raised, given its own printed invoice number, and added to what the client has left to settle. What the workplace experience manager sees afterwards is a late charge standing on the contract and a larger unsettled invoice balance.

### What the function proves

`post_late_charge_719c9a63` raises a late charge on a workplace cafe management contract whose cafe invoicing has stood unpaid. One call books the charge of the amount given onto that contract's ledger under the late charge subtype, dates it the day of the call, records it against the billing period named, gives it its own printed invoice number and raises the contract's unsettled invoice balance by the same amount.

### How it is invoked

The function is unlocked on the client services desk and then called as `post_late_charge_719c9a63`, once, against the contract carrying the unpaid cafe invoicing.

### What is passed

- `cafe_contract_id` — the reference number of the workplace cafe management contract the late charge is raised on; it is returned by the cafe contract lookup for the client.
- `late_charge_usd` — the late charge being raised, in USD, written as a decimal number to 2 decimal places; it is stored to 2 decimal places exactly as given and must be a positive amount.
- `service_period` — the billing period the late charge is recorded against, written as a calendar month in the form YYYY-MM with no day part.

### What comes back

A single confirmation sentence in plain text naming the contract reference charged, the late charge in USD to 2 decimal places, the billing period it was recorded against, the posting day as YYYY-MM-DD, the printed invoice number of the new posting in the form INV-CF- followed by 6 digits, and the contract's unsettled invoice balance in USD to 2 decimal places after the charge. Receiving that sentence is what shows the charge stands.
